gloss: to exhaust all options; to run out of ideas

definitions.gloss: to exhaust all options; to run out of ideas; to have no more measures left
definitions.explanation: A situation in which every possible strategy or solution has been tried and nothing remains. Expresses a sense of helplessness after having done everything one can.

examples.japanese: {万策尽|ばんさくつ}きて{途方|とほう}に{暮|く}れた。
examples.english: Having exhausted all options, I was at a complete loss.

examples.japanese: {交渉|こうしょう}は{難航|なんこう}し、{万策尽|ばんさくつ}きたかに{見|み}えたが、{最後|さいご}に{妥協案|だきょうあん}が{見|み}つかった。
examples.english: Negotiations were difficult and it seemed like all options had been exhausted, but a compromise was found at the last moment.

notes:
Composed of {万策|ばんさく} (all measures/strategies, literally 'ten thousand plans') + {尽|つ}きる (to be exhausted, to run out). An expressive set phrase conveying total helplessness.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {万策尽|ばんさくつ}きた: all options exhausted (past tense, most common form)
- {万策尽|ばんさくつ}きて: having exhausted all options (conjunctive)
- もはや{万策尽|ばんさくつ}きた: there are truly no more options left

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {手詰|てづ}まり: deadlock, stalemate — a situation where no progress can be made; less dramatic
- {八方塞|はっぽうふさ}がり: blocked in all directions — every path is closed off; emphasizes being trapped
- お{手上|てあ}げ: giving up, throwing in the towel — a more casual expression of helplessness

USAGE:
A dramatic, literary expression often used at moments of crisis. Common in news reporting, fiction, and speeches. The phrase {万策尽|ばんさくつ}きた is particularly well-known from sports and political commentary.
